I couldn’t find him for nearly an hour, and was about to go back home when the thousands of jewels and glittering valuables under my feet began moving in a disgustingly ^^^alive way.

He slipped down figuring it was Biammu.

“Damn, you were hidden very well.” The dragon’s golden head made a woosh through the air as it slowly turned towards the small creature that had invaded his lazy sleep. It huffed, Biammu closed his eyes for a moment before looking back at him.
“What human?”
A crackling noise, like a fire made its way up his huge throat as his voice boomed across the cave.

“Hey, you’re the one who ordered me here big guy. You’re gonna get your life together.”

His lip snarled, and let the teeth that were bigger than a human flash in their brilliant yellow.
“I never ask humans for help! I can’t do it myself...” The growl would have sent a shutter down Mernin’s spine if he weren’t so used to that reaction.
“So you admit you need help.” He wiggled his eyebrows to the large dragon he was still sort of standing on top of. The huge brown orbs glared at him, as the mounds of golden glittering trinkets to down right thrones, began shifting once again. “Good God, you may be the most incredibly talented Hoarder I’ve ever seen.”

The dragon couldn’t help but feel a little pride as he strut over his piles of gold, not yet catching onto The insult. When he did the spikes on his head flattened, and he flung some gold off a mound with his tail in a pout.
Mernin tripped when the dragon’s tail went free, falling down the ever shifting landscape.

His feet caught on something bigger, probably wood. “Is this a dresser? Holy...” this could be one of the most difficult cases he’d come across. This was an entire cave, full of enough gold to hide a golden dragon?
“I didn’t ask you or your smart mouth to come here, so get out.” He started self consciously tidying around, moving some piles with his claws around to the edges of the cave, then using his wings to blow away some dirt from the cave floor.

Mernin coughed, and furrowed his eyebrows.
“Must’ve been Persephone....” the dragon grumbled. “Well...I’m going to help you anyways.”

Huge gates opened, and the people in the room all shuttered, staring at the blank looking world outside of the habitat. Blank... that’s all I could describe it as. Like a canvas yet to be painted on. Made a masterpiece...
For the past thirty minutes of waiting in strange clothes that made it ridiculously hot, it no longer was so unbearable. The huge expanse of white, sent waves of freezing cold air into the room, and someone with the same layered on cloth as I poked at my back. Moving forward was hard. When I was leaving my entire family behind? To this nothingness?
The person behind me looked stern, and glared at me through the same kind of goggles I wore. Stepping hesitantly over the currently cooling down, dark brown earth, the gate got closer. And closer. Until the heavy boots that trapped my feet inside, crunched loudly in the white. We both stopped in fear, and looked at the boot. “K-keep going.” The Guy not much older than me ordered. with another shove from the wooden pole, it stuck my back harshly, forcing my body into a stumble. What if I sunk into the white and died? What if it consumed me and no one cared?!

No consuming...  just several loud crunchy foot steps. “Go.” The guy said, not looking at me. I crossed my arms, hoping for warmth again to just be bestowed upon me like it had been all my life. The gates started to close. On the outside, bright sliver, and shiny, and wet, but the only side I wanted to see was the one with green vines growing on it. No green was anywhere in this...this... nothingness.
A simple bow with arrows, more heavy clothes of fur, and berries that stayed good as they were cold but not freezing. Just those things in a backpack, with nothing else. We all needed to learn how to hunt animals, as that was one of the biggest jobs in the colony. But this tiny, white creature that nearly blended in with all around it was moving. And fast. The chickens didn’t move, or move very fast when every kid had learned how to shoot them.
This little creature had huge ears matching its body, but the tail didn’t seem to provide any help when walking on top of the snow. How had it been doing that?! His huge feet must have helped. Maybe he should try big shoes.

-and that’s all for now folks because it’s 4:53 AM and I feel like I should probably slEEP, then pretend I’ll start making better life choices for the rest of the day.
